product_context.problem_statement: Fleet safety operators need a timely, evidence-rich way to identify when a developmental autonomous vehicle may be outside its approved operating design domain, without delegating vehicle-control responsibility to the console.
product_context.value_hypothesis: Earlier, explainable safety escalations will reduce unsafe autonomous driving exposure while keeping only reviewed vehicles available for supervised test routes.
in_scope: Decision support for human pause, manual-takeover, and incident escalation on pre-approved test routes
Operator-facing perception, ODD, sensor-health, and alert-freshness evidence
A console safety latch that prevents return-to-test authorization until human review is recorded
non_goals: Vehicle steering, braking, throttle, or route selection
Automatic vehicle-control commands or a substitute for the safety driver's immediate manual-control responsibility
Facial recognition, biometric inference, or raw cabin-video retention
product_context.user_journey_moment: During supervised public-road testing, immediately before or during an ODD, perception, or driver-attention alert.
product_context.fallback_experience: On an out-of-policy ODD, critical sensor, alert-integrity, or operator-availability signal, the console latches an unsafe status and shows a manual-takeover/pause instruction. The safety driver takes manual control without waiting for a remote recommendation; the remote operator and safety desk receive the evidence, and the console cannot mark the vehicle authorized to return to autonomous testing until a Fleet Safety Lead records approval after review.

system_profile.purpose: Surface current, safety-relevant evidence to help authorized humans instruct a manual takeover or pause an AV test before unsafe continued operation; the system cannot issue vehicle-control commands.
system_profile.decision_impact: A recommendation can cause a human to pause a public-road test; failure to escalate can expose pedestrians, cyclists, passengers, and road users to injury.
data_types: Camera-derived object, trajectory, confidence, and freshness labels
Safety-driver availability signals; no facial recognition, biometric inference, or raw cabin-video retention
system_profile.deployment_context: Research-only simulation and closed-course scenarios now; a proposed limited, daylight, supervised public-road test fleet on named routes in Vietnam later. No passenger service or driverless deployment is in scope.

system_boundary.model: Rule-assisted risk-ranking model with confidence thresholds that require independent validation and cannot issue vehicle-control commands
system_boundary.application: Operator console that displays alert evidence, data freshness, a manual-takeover/pause recommendation, and a return-to-test safety latch
downstream_decisions: Safety driver's manual takeover or human pause

industry_risk_snapshot.rationale: A missed, delayed, stale, or poorly understood escalation during public-road testing can contribute to serious injury or death and may be hard to reverse. The proposed pilot constrains scale, but pedestrians and other non-customers cannot opt out. Sensitive-data risk is scored 3 because route-linked telemetry and camera-derived labels can still concern road users and safety drivers even though face recognition, biometric inference, and raw cabin-video retention are out of scope. The NTSB Tempe report shows that operator attention, system limits, and safety governance matter together.

vietnam.rationale: Law 134/2025 applies to AI activities in Vietnam. Decision 33/2026's transport category may apply only if the final integrated system controls the vehicle or operates without continuous human supervision; SafeRoute's stated decision-support boundary and continuous safety driver leave that unresolved. Before a public-road pilot, counsel must document classification, provider/deployer roles, transport-test authorization, any notification or conformity-assessment duty, incident duties, and personal-data basis, retention, and transfer controls.

eu.rationale: A prospective EU assessment is unresolved. Article 6 may be relevant only if the final intended purpose makes SafeRoute an AI safety component of a product within Annex I and the product requires third-party conformity assessment. The current decision-support boundary, vehicle integration, provider/deployer role, market-placement facts, and applicable dates have not been established; this is not a compliance conclusion.

legal_classification.other_markets: No market assessment is made beyond Vietnam and a prospective EU comparison; expansion requires a jurisdiction-specific review.

product_metrics.success_kpi: For each independently observed research test week, 100% of independently adjudicated critical ODD, perception, or operator-availability scenarios present a complete evidence bundle (ODD state, sensor health, alert freshness, confidence, and driver-availability state) to the designated operator before a documented pause-or-continue disposition; report the scenario count and scenario mix.
product_metrics.risk_kri: Per supervised research test week: 0 confirmed critical missed escalations and 0 alert-evidence-integrity failures; report the numerator, independently adjudicated critical-scenario denominator, route kilometers where applicable, and false-alert burden. Any non-zero result pauses the affected route or software version for investigation.
product_metrics.guardrail_metric: Hard stop: 0 autonomous test kilometers while any critical ODD, sensor, alert-integrity, or human-operator-availability condition is outside approved policy. On detection, the safety driver takes manual control and the route remains paused until independent review records a safe return-to-test decision.
product_metrics.review_cadence: Safety review weekly and before each route or ODD expansion; re-review and re-classify immediately after a collision, near miss, KRI or guardrail breach, material model, threshold, data, sensor, vendor, vehicle, route, or market change.

release_blockers: GAP-01: ODD, alert-integrity, and manual-takeover safety case is not accepted
GAP-02: Independent scenario, workload, and alert-burden evaluation is incomplete
GAP-03: Vietnam AI classification, transport authorization, and incident-governance gate is open
GAP-04: Vietnam personal-data roles, retention, and transfer gate is open
GAP-05: Independent post-incident restart-veto control is not demonstrated
release_conditions: Research is limited to simulation and closed-course scenarios using synthetic or de-identified data; no public-road autonomous test kilometers or live road-user imagery are permitted.
No public-road pilot until GAP-01 through GAP-05 are done, the independent assessor accepts the evidence, and the Chief Safety Officer accepts residual risk.
Any critical missed escalation, alert-evidence-integrity failure, safety incident, or legal reclassification pauses scope expansion.
release_decision.next_review_trigger: 2026-10-15; any collision or near-miss investigation; KRI or guardrail breach; legal reclassification; or material vehicle, sensor, vendor, route, data-flow, or market change.
release_decision.residual_risk_rationale: Severity remains 5 because a missed or corrupted alert can still expose non-consenting road users to physical harm, and a safety driver may not be ready merely because an alert was acknowledged. The proposed controls are planned rather than demonstrated, so their residual likelihood is not yet acceptable. Research-only is appropriate until the safety case, independent scenario evidence, legal gates, and independent restart authority are complete.
